citations.assessment: The Nehardea qualifier applies to the two rulings on tefillin in the adjacent segments.
The explicitly named Dimi of Nehardea rules on meat slaughtered on Shabbat for a sick person.
The concern about pairs is attributed to Dimi of Nehardea; the surrounding tradition also uses a shorter name.
The passage gives the named Dimi’s ruling on whether to suspect an erring court.
A drowned man is retrieved three days after the drowning. Dimi permits his wife to remarry. The wound and swelling discussion is the anonymous argument that follows.
The merchandise in this episode is dried figs carried by ship.
The local article quotes this exact incident and its larger context.
The Bavli says Dimi went up to Nehardea and sent a retraction. This occurrence gives only the short name; the quoted Shmuel article discusses the idiom.
Nehardea is explicitly named in applying the comparison to a frontier town. The use of this fact to explain ascent remains conjectural.
The rain discussion contrasts the upper and lower regions. The place-name assignment is in the geographical explanation cited under Shmuel.
The cross-reference gives the same question and quotes the explanation about the Euphrates and the relative locations.
Amemar transmits Dimi’s named teaching and is the addressee of Mar Zutra’s reply.
The chronology gives the three-year term under the short name and records differing death-year notices. It does not specify which Dimi; the article expressly leaves him unidentified.
